newsitem.title: USA: Republican takes lead in Washington state race.
newsitem.headline: Republican takes lead in Washington state race.

text.p: The boost provided by Washington state voters to congressional Democrats last week appeared to weaken Tuesday as absentee ballots gave freshman Republican Linda Smith the lead in a still-undecided race.
Smith, a leader of the 1994 Republican revolution, was leading Democratic challenger Brian Baird in southeast Washington by 700 votes, according to the latest unofficial results.
In another race north of Seattle, Democratic challenger Kevin Quigley maintained a 1,200-vote lead over first-term Republican Representative Jack Metcalf, down from 2,500 on election night.
Baird, a psychology professor and political newcomer, had been declared the winner by major media outlets Wednesday, but Smith took the lead after election officials began counting absentee ballots.
The counting process resumed Tuesday after a government holiday, but county officials had until Nov. 20 to certify the results.
With about 10,000 ballots left to be counted, Smith had 117,038 votes or 50.15 percent to Baird's 116,338 or 49.85 percent.
Washington state law provides an automatic recount for any race where the margin is within 0.5 percent of the total, and neither candidate was ready to declare victory or concede defeat.
The race was among a handful of congressional contests around the country that remained undecided a week after Election Day.
So far Democrats have won 204 seats in the House of Representatives -- six more than in the previous Congress -- but Republicans retained control of the 435-seat chamber with at least 225 seats.

The Washington races were watched closely because the state elected six freshman Republicans in 1994, more than any other state. Among them was George Nethercutt, who beat former Speaker Tom Foley and went on to win a second term last week.
Representative Randy Tate, the youngest member of the freshman Republican class of 1994, lost to Decmoractic state Sen. Adam Smith in a suburban district south of Seattle.
